> only found a thread like this from 2002 (didn't look that hard ;) )

Well, see, the reason threads like this don't come up so much is that
it is really hard to come up with "the best cards" for this game,
'cause of the way it works. So you gotta kinda specificy what you are
looking for. For example, my list of the "most effective staple cards"
would be:

-Govern
-Deflection
-Conditioning
-Telepathic Misdirection
-Lost in Crowds
-Kine Resources Contested
-Wake/On the Qui
-Blood Doll
-Dreams
-Minion Tap

In the sense of "these are the cards that are most likely to show up
in a given field of decks, 'cause they are really good for their cost
and tend to enable entire strategies". I think it is notable that 8.5
of these are cards from the original set, and all but one of them are
commons. And 3 of them are Dominate.

I could come up with a list of "best cards for combat decks" or "best
cards for bleed decks" or "best master cards" or whatever. But a
general "best cards in the game" is a really hard list to invent.

-Peter

IME it's a moot point, because against POT they're all maneuvers ;)

> Never was a big Tremere/Tha guy. So I will have to take your word for
> it. There's no way you could explain it or give examples? Old tech:
> Theft, press, Walk of Flame. What's the new tech that makes Press to
> End so much better?

Press, Walk of Flame is unreliable at best and occasionally gets stuck
in your hand (though it is very funny). You can build an efficient
combat package using fewer cards if you ignore the second-round
stuff. When you have given up on the Walk of Flame, Apportation makes
less sense. Since your combat is more defensive, your vampires stay
alive longer to implement whatever strategy your deck is built for,
and you have more cards available in the deck for that strategy.

And things go wrong in combat. Thaumaturgy is second-tier, and the
minions who weild it are typically vulnerable to hitback. Apportation
gives you offense potential at a great cost: you won't be able to save
yourself from continued Carrion Crows or guns or some devastating Trap
combo just by pressing to end.

> And the Press to End is that much better than say, Perfect Clarity?

Only in that the card is more widely applicable. Perfect Clarity
doesn't go into a deck as often as one of the maneuvers even though
the effect is clearly stronger.

> On a different topic (sorry), is it worth it to explore rush THA, or is

People try all the time, but usually with wacky discipline combos like:

-Tha/Pot (IG backed Blood Fury strikes)
-Tha/Cel (for manuvers/additionals/Psyche)

Messages.Author: Dasein
Messages.Body:
> On a different topic (sorry), is it worth it to explore rush THA, or is
> that a non-starter due to lack of protection from hit-back?

Lack of protection isn't the only problem. Other problems:
- fairly reliant on manuevers / presses, making the combo chains
fairly long and precarious.
- Inability to deal with dodge / combat ends (except via support
disciplines, see below)
- Inability to deliver large amounts of damage on the first round,
even assuming you can chain a good combo together (e.g. Pot has I.S. /
manuever / thrown lid; Tha can't do much on the first round at all)

Thaumaturgy's general support disciplines are Aus and Dom. While those
are great overall disciplines (arguably the best in the game), they
generally aren't much use in combat. However, each of those has a way
to deal with S:CE, one of the weaknesses of Tha combat.
Thoughts Betrayed is the better since it stops them playing SCE in the
first place, though it is expensive. Theft will help make up for this,
but again you are open to hitback, and if that hitback takes the form
of a punch for 4 from Beast with a signpost, then you're in big poo
(and that's before you get disarmed).
Telepathic Tracking is less strong since they can S:CE on the next
round again if they have one. It also has the risk of restarting a
combat with an effect you are not enjoying (e.g. Crows, DotB at super,
Weather Control, etc.) For this reason it is generally played by
Tzimisce in a deck that itself plays Crows (and/or other 'each round'
nastiness like KrakKiss / Horrid Form).
Both of those cost blood, boo, whereas IG is free, and thus full of
win.

As Peter said, for all these reasons, Tha combat is usually bolted on
to another combat module (pot/for, pot/cel, etc.) rather than used by
Tremere / !Tremere as a fundamental combat discipline itself. I've
played around with it and found it be quite ineffective on its own
(though perhaps one day I will make a pot/tha or maybe even pot/tha/
pro deck and have fun punching people for 4 unpreventable aggravated
damage in a grapple).

Messages.Author: J
Messages.Body:
> Plan brown Tremere Rush (using just Tha/Dom/Aus or whatever) can
> certainly work in a low combat environment, but will get foiled by S:CE
> (unless you pack a lot of Telepathic Tracking) and often just mangled by
> opposing light combat (i.e. guns and Ivory Bows and whatever).

I don't know. You can generally get decent low-mid caps with THA, or
even lower if you want to pack discipline cards. And with small vamps
who can wake to flick afterwards, you have the ability to interate
those S:CE guys into torpor or the ash pile.

I've got a deck that's ok along these lines. Trap, h1, thefts and
walks. Sure, S:CE gets around it a bit, but I play the deck very
aggressively. Rushing or bleeding with pretty much all my minions all
the time. It has taken GW, and taken them in tournaments. It came
3rd at the Aus LCQ last year which had a surprising amount of combat.

The first table it sat on was a 4 player. Me - Blood Brothers - cel/
POT trophy - !Ventrue with hitback. And it swept that table. Sure,
it got toasted in a later round by the eventual winner playing !
Brujah, but there wasn't a table that I didn't sit on where there
wasn't plenty of combat.

I definately don't think that you can play big cap THA combat though -
unless you are definately packing Thoughts, because your actions just
don't have the effect that you can get with other combat disciplines.
So, in the bigger decks - it's better to play THA defensively.

--> J

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
On Apr 13, 10:45 am, "Reyda !" <Rey...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I'd remove the Telepathic misdirection though (less effective at the
> inferior) but add Ivory Bow instead :)

Heh. See, Telepathic Misdirection is the only other relaible source of
bleed bounce in the game. And as we all know, bleed bounce is
*incredibly* effective as a defense. To that point that many people
don't even build decks unless they can fit in bleed bounce. Your
options for bleed bounce are, pretty much, Deflection (Redirection is
ok, but considerably less useful than Deflection, and in the majority
of cases, the 1 blood cost for the Deflection is going to seem
insignificant compared to the increased usefulness) and Telepathic
Misdirection (My Enemy's Enemy is also ok, but it tends to be used as
a "+1 intercept card that I can use as bounce in a pinch" as opposed
to the other way around for TM) .

That, and Telepathic Misdirection is a lot more flexible than
Deflection--you can play TM for intercept if you need to and it is
still a useful card as a result in the 2 player end game. I mean,
yeah, I agree that Deflection is better in an absolute sense than
Telepathic Misdirection for bleed bounce (i.e. given the choice, most
of the time I'll take Deflection over Telepathic Misdirection for a
bleed bounce defense), but as cards of utility go in the grand scheme,
Telepathic Misdirection is one of the best in the game. As it is good
bleed bounce.

-Peter

I've got a "doozy" to add to your list Robert.
Esteem....now inform me if I missed the boat on this card..but isn't
it totally wallpaper?

Anyways here is my top 10 best (reasonably speaking) list.

1. Blood Doll
2. WWEF
3. Govern
4. Telepathic Misdirection/Deflection
5. Minion Tap
6. Voter Cap
7. Kindred Spirits
8. 2nd Tradition
9. Parity Shift
10. Clan Specific Pool Gaining Locations (ie.) Art Museum

My list as quickly as I made it, could very easly be changed almost
daily. But everything on it has a mild theme. They can all preserve
your pool, or get you more.
KS lets a bleed deck continue to bleed and gain pool, not wasting
other actions to gain pool. I wanted to add stealth and intercept
cards, but they accentuate those base actions that are so vital.
Actions are the most important in this game to me.
